summary.text: Chris Pappas is the Democratic nominee for the open New Hampshire U.S. Senate seat. A Manchester native who co-owns his family's restaurant, he served in the state House, as Hillsborough County treasurer and on the Executive Council before winning New Hampshire's 1st District U.S. House seat in 2018. He is running for the seat Sen. Jeanne Shaheen is not seeking to hold.

paragraphs.text: Pappas was born in Manchester, New Hampshire, in 1980, and is a descendant of Greek immigrants. He attended public schools in Manchester and earned a bachelor's degree in government from Harvard University in 2002.
He is a co-owner of his family's restaurant, the Puritan Backroom in Manchester, which his campaign website describes as a landmark business he ran before entering Congress.

Pappas was elected to the New Hampshire House of Representatives after graduating and served two terms, from 2002 to 2006. He then served as treasurer of Hillsborough County from 2007 to 2011 and as a member of the state Executive Council from 2013 to 2019.
He has represented New Hampshire's 1st Congressional District in the U.S. House since 2019. Ballotpedia notes that he was the first openly gay U.S. House member elected from New Hampshire.
In the House, Pappas serves on the Veterans' Affairs and Transportation and Infrastructure committees, and he has served as co-chair of the Congressional Equality Caucus.
He won the September 8, 2026, Democratic primary for U.S. Senate with 64.6% of the vote, ahead of Karishma Manzur (33.2%).
According to his campaign website, Pappas lives in Manchester with his husband, Vann.
